anchor.note: The page only gives a range for sigma and never says what it denotes (an auxiliary exponent with (s/W)^nu <= m^(nu sigma)); no earlier page binds it with this meaning.

gaps.quote: which only the paper's later division algorithm needs, not its main multiplication theorem
gaps.note: False. The recursion with exponent lambda<1 and the resulting d^{lambda'} layer bound are used in the main multiplication algorithm: the paper's introduction says the cost O(V d^{lambda'}) is for 'the layouts used in the multiplication algorithm' (lines 93-99), the power saving gives the O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) bound of Theorem 1 (line 386, section at line 2393), and the exponents tau, sigma, lambda, lambda' are fixed for the multiplication proof (line 4010). The division section (line 4996) only reuses them.

gaps.quote: Here $m=2$ is the factor by which the parameter grows
gaps.note: The paper does not fix m=2. m is the dimension of the fixed binary label space of the network (line 2237), the parameter grows by that factor m, and the construction needs a large m (m=1,000,000 at line 2470; requires s<Wm with fixed m,W>=2 at line 1468). The page's own subset-intersection network is not available for m=2; only the later example uses m=2 as an illustration.

Does not follow. The leaf bound f^sigma d^{vartheta(1-sigma)} is not at most f^lambda: since only sigma<lambda is assumed and f can be as large as d, it is d^{sigma+vartheta(1-sigma)}, which can exceed d^lambda (e.g. vartheta=1/2, sigma=0.79, lambda=0.8 gives 0.895>0.8). The paper (lines 2425-2426, 2437-2445) keeps the leaf term as O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) and absorbs it only in the final bound O(d^{lambda'}) with lambda' > max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}.

gaps.quote: Each leaf is handled by one kernel per chunk, at cost $O(f/m^\nu)$.
gaps.note: The page never says what a kernel is (the paper's individual selected-bit C butterfly kernel applied to one chunk, line 2260 ff.), nor why one kernel costs O(1) per bit of volume so that a leaf costs O(f/m^nu) per unit volume.

gaps.quote: The outside work is a fixed number of address-field row additions.
gaps.note: The page does not say what a row addition is or why the node's outside work (changes of basis, gates, corrections) is a fixed number of them. Its stated cost O(V(u^tau+1)) is not derived from the interchange cost O(Vu^tau) given just before; it comes from a separate lemma of the paper (lines 2004-2010, 2226) with extra hypotheses.
